text:
maria_support: FYI - ACME reporting lots of 401s + huge latency for EU users since ~06:40 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-west and are seeing unexpected billing spikes. I'm collecting logs.
acme_prod: Confirmed from our side — EU customers (DE/FR) get '401 Unauthorized' and requests show x-edge-pop: usw2-1. Example request id: req-987654. Started ~06:38.
jason_eng: Can you paste the full request headers for one of those req ids (masked token is fine). Also are these browser clients or server-to-server calls?
acme_prod: Browser and mobile. Example headers (sanitized): `x-edge-pop: usw2-1`, `x-client-ip: 88.123.45.67`, `x-geo-country: DE`, `x-auth-token: token-***`
li_netops: If EU IPs are resolving to a US pop, likely culprit is GeoDB parity or an upstream resolver returning wrong answers (ISP proxy / EDNS behavior). Any pattern on ISPs?
acme_prod: Mostly Vodafone DE and some corporate proxies. We ran a dig from a couple affected clients and the CNAME chain ended up at our us-west LB.
paul_sre: Repro checklist for their ops: 1) `dig +short @<their_resolver> acme.redwood.ai` 2) `dig +short @8.8.8.8 acme.redwood.ai +edns=0` 3) curl their client to capture `x-edge-pop` and `x-auth-region` headers. Also get a traceroute from the client to the edge IP.
maria_support: Example dig snippet we asked them to run:
```sh
# from affected client's network
dig +short A acme.redwood.ai @<their_resolver>
dig +short CNAME acme.redwood.ai
``` 
They returned CNAME -> lb-usw2.internal.redwood with TTL 300.
deploy-bot: geoip-db-sync:prod completed on some clusters at 06:35 UTC, but sync job failed for eu-edge-cluster-3 (S3 503 during artifact fetch). Automatic retry scheduled.
jason_eng: That aligns — eu-edge-cluster-3 had a stale GeoDB and used default mapping -> US region. Fallback routing + token region-binding causes auth mismatch and double-charge behaviour in billing pipeline.
li_netops: Mitigation options: 1) force a geo-db reload on eu-edge clusters; 2) lower DNS edge TTL temporarily (30s) and bump CNAME to force resolver refresh; 3) ask affected customers to flush client resolver caches if possible. We can also push a transient config to accept cross-region tokens `auth.allow-cross-region-temp=true` for a short window.
paul_sre: I'm rolling a reload to eu-edge-cluster-3 now and will trigger the S3 retry. Also will add an active health check to reject stale geodb instances earlier.
acme_prod: Can you provide exact commands we can run to verify once you say it's fixed? Our ops team needs step-by-step.
maria_support: Sent quick verification steps to your inbox but paste here as well: 1) run `dig +edns=0 @<local_resolver> acme.redwood.ai` and check CNAME ends with `eu-lb.internal.redwood`. 2) curl example: `curl -s -I https://acme.redwood.ai/health -H "Host: acme.redwood.ai"` and verify `x-edge-pop: euc1-2` and `x-auth-region: eu`. 3) if still seeing US pop, collect `traceroute -n <edge_ip>` and `dig +trace` output and upload.
jason_eng: GeoDB reload complete (eu-edge-cluster-3) at 06:51 UTC, purged local resolver cache on that cluster. Pushed a targeted DNS TTL change for affected records to 30s for 15 minutes to accelerate propagation.
maria_support: Passing update to ACME — please hold billing dispute for 1 hour while we verify. I'll log timeline and affected req ids for billing team.
acme_prod: Will hold on billing action for now. We'll run the verification steps and post results in 20m.
jason_eng: Follow-up: we also found the sync job didn't surface transient S3 503s to the orchestration alert; adding retry+alert. Will post a short postmortem once billing queue cleared.
maria_support: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open until ACME confirms. :thumbsup:
acme_prod: Verified — after ~10m most clients now land in EU pop and 401s gone. Sending list of 120 affected request ids to billing. Thanks.
jason_eng: Noted. I'll follow up with a short incident note and the fix timeline. Closing once billing ack.
